claim: HFD-fed mice had higher body weight by 3 weeks compared to controls.
source: HFD-fed mice had higher body weight and impaired fasting blood glucose by 3 weeks, compared to controls (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by body weight measurements shown in Figure 1A across feeding durations.

claim: HFD-fed mice had impaired fasting blood glucose by 3 weeks compared to controls.
source: HFD-fed mice had higher body weight and impaired fasting blood glucose by 3 weeks, compared to controls (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: Supported by fasting blood glucose measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Body weight continued to rise with prolonged HFD feeding.
source: Body weight and hyperglycemia continued to rise with prolonged feeding.
evidence: Supported by longitudinal body weight data in Figure 1A.

claim: Hyperglycemia continued to rise with prolonged HFD feeding.
source: Body weight and hyperglycemia continued to rise with prolonged feeding.
evidence: Supported by fasting blood glucose measurements across time points in Figure 1B.

claim: HFD-fed mice displayed higher EWAT weight at 3 weeks.
source: HFD-fed mice also displayed higher EWAT weight (Figure 1C) and inter-scapular brown AT (BAT) weight at 3 weeks (not shown).
evidence: Supported by EWAT weight measurements shown in Figure 1C.

claim: HFD-fed mice displayed higher inter-scapular brown AT (BAT) weight at 3 weeks.
source: HFD-fed mice also displayed higher EWAT weight (Figure 1C) and inter-scapular brown AT (BAT) weight at 3 weeks (not shown).
evidence: Stated in text but data not shown in manuscript.

claim: Cross-sectional tibia and femur bone histology showed an increase in BMA size by 3 weeks of HFD.
source: Cross-sectional tibia and femur bone histology visualized via H & E and Oil Red O staining showed an increase in BMA size by 3 weeks and an increase in BMA number by 8 weeks of HFD (Figure 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis and quantification in Figure 1D-G.

claim: Cross-sectional tibia and femur bone histology showed an increase in BMA number by 8 weeks of HFD.
source: Cross-sectional tibia and femur bone histology visualized via H & E and Oil Red O staining showed an increase in BMA size by 3 weeks and an increase in BMA number by 8 weeks of HFD (Figure 1D–G).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis and quantification in Figure 1D-G.

claim: 3 weeks of HFD sufficed to induce whole body metabolic disturbance and augmented adiposity in peripheral tissues and in the BM.
source: This indicated that 3 weeks of HFD sufficed to induce whole body metabolic disturbance and augmented adiposity in peripheral tissues and in the BM.
evidence: Inferred from the combined observations of increased body weight, hyperglycemia, EWAT weight, BAT weight, and BMA size at 3 weeks.

claim: Myeloid cells in the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) of AT were not elevated until 8 weeks of HFD.
source: Although total EWAT weight increased by 3 weeks, myeloid cells in the stromal vascular fraction (SVF) of AT were not elevated until 8 weeks of HFD, as indicated by gene expression of the general myeloid marker Itgam (encoding CD11b) and monocyte markers Gr1- CD115+ CD11b+ Ly6C+ (determined by flow cytometry) (Figure 2A and D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression and flow cytometry data in Figure 2A and D.

claim: AT macrophages were not elevated at 3 weeks of HFD but were at 8 weeks.
source: Similarly, AT macrophages, assessed by gene expression of the AT macrophage marker Adgre1 (encoding F4/80) and by flow cytometry counting of CD11b+ Ly6C- F4/80+ macrophages in the SVF were not elevated at 3 weeks of HFD but were at 8 weeks (Figure 2B and E).
evidence: Supported by gene expression and flow cytometry data in Figure 2B and E.

claim: Pro-inflammatory myeloid markers were higher in the SVF by 8 weeks of HFD relative to control diet, but not at 3 weeks.
source: Further, gene expression of the pro-inflammatory myeloid marker Itgax (encoding CD11c) and surface detection of the pro-inflammatory markers CD11b+ Ly6C- F4/80+ CD11c+ were also higher in the SVF by 8 weeks of HFD relative to control diet, but not at 3 weeks (Figure 2C and F).
evidence: Supported by gene expression and flow cytometry data in Figure 2C and F.

claim: Gene expression of the embryonically-conserved tissue-resident AT macrophage markers Timd4 and Marco was not elevated at 3 or at 8 weeks and only rose at 18 weeks of HFD.
source: Of note, gene expression of the embryonically-conserved tissue-resident AT macrophage markers Timd4 and Marco (Beattie et al., 2016; Gibbings et al., 2015) was not elevated at 3 or at 8 weeks and only rose at 18 weeks of HFD (Figure 2G–H).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 2G-H and cited references.

claim: The gain in AT macrophages at 8 weeks of HFD is unlikely due to proliferation of resident macrophages and instead likely results from monocyte recruitment from the circulation.
source: This indicates that the gain in AT macrophages at 8 weeks of HFD is unlikely due to proliferation of resident macrophages and instead likely results from monocyte recruitment from the circulation.
evidence: Inferred from the observation that resident macrophage markers were not elevated at 8 weeks.

claim: Total BM monocytes increased at 3 weeks and continued to rise by 8 and 18 weeks of HFD.
source: In the BM, total monocytes, gated via the Gr1- CD115+ CD11b+ Ly6C+ markers, increased at 3 weeks and continued to rise by 8 and 18 weeks of HFD (Figure 2I).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2I.

claim: At 3 weeks into the feeding study, Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes represented about 40% of the total BM monocyte population in the control diet group.
source: At 3 weeks into the feeding study, Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes represented about 40% of the total BM monocyte population in the control diet group, whereas HFD promoted a higher proportion of Ly6Clow monocytes (Figure 2J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: HFD promoted a higher proportion of Ly6Clow monocytes at 3 weeks.
source: At 3 weeks into the feeding study, Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes represented about 40% of the total BM monocyte population in the control diet group, whereas HFD promoted a higher proportion of Ly6Clow monocytes (Figure 2J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: By 8 weeks of HFD there was a marked shift, whereby the relative proportion of Ly6Clow monocytes in the total monocyte population was lower and that of Ly6Chigh monocytes was higher than under the control diet.
source: However, by 8 weeks of HFD there was a marked shift, whereby the relative proportion of Ly6Clow monocytes in the total monocyte population was lower and that of Ly6Chigh monocytes was higher than under the control diet (Figure 2J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: The differences in monocyte subset proportions were more prominent by 18 weeks of HFD feeding.
source: These differences were more prominent by 18 weeks of HFD feeding (Figure 2J).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: HFD favoured monocytosis at 3 weeks, with a subsequent and prominent switch towards tissue invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes at 8 weeks that continued into 18 weeks of HFD.
source: Collectively, these findings revealed that, in the BM, HFD favoured monocytosis at 3 weeks, with a subsequent and prominent switch towards tissue invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes at 8 weeks that continued into 18 weeks of HFD.
evidence: Summary of flow cytometry data from Figure 2I-J.

claim: Singer et al., 2014 demonstrated an increase in BM monocytosis and elevated monocyte progenitor cells with 18 weeks of HFD, that persisted after BM transplantation into chow-fed recipients.
source: Singer et al., 2014 also demonstrated an increase in BM monocytosis and elevated monocyte progenitor cells with 18 weeks of HFD, that persisted after BM transplantation into chow-fed recipients.
evidence: Cited from Singer et al., 2014 study.

claim: We did not observe statistically significant increases in monocyte progenitor and stem cells at any time point analyzed.
source: In the present study, while we clearly recorded an earlier and continuing rise in total monocytes in HFD-fed mice (Figure 2I), we did not observe statistically significant increases in monocyte progenitor and stem cells at any time point analyzed (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-C.

claim: Ly6Clow monocytes have a higher mitochondrial membrane potential than Ly6Chigh monocytes in the control mice.
source: The results exhibit that Ly6Clow monocytes have a higher mitochondrial membrane potential than Ly6Chigh monocytes in the control mice (Figure 3A–C).
evidence: Supported by MitoTracker Red CMXRos flow cytometry data in Figure 3A-C.

claim: 3 weeks of HFD reduced the mitochondrial membrane potential in both monocyte subsets.
source: Strikingly, 3 weeks of HFD reduced the mitochondrial membrane potential in both monocyte subsets indicated by the left-ward shift in the MitoTracker Red CMXRos peak (Figure 3A).
evidence: Supported by MitoTracker Red CMXRos flow cytometry data in Figure 3A.

claim: The HFD-induced effects on mitochondrial membrane potential were more pronounced by 8 and 18 weeks of HFD.
source: The HFD-induced effects were more pronounced by 8 and 18 weeks of HFD (Figure 3B and C).
evidence: Supported by MitoTracker Red CMXRos flow cytometry data in Figure 3B and C.

claim: There was a gradual lowering in the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) of Ly6Clow monocytes with HFD.
source: The results revealed a gradual lowering in the oxygen consumption rate (OCR) of Ly6Clow monocytes with HFD (Figure 3D–I).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3D-I.

claim: At 18 weeks, the OCR of the Ly6Clow monocytes was significantly lowered by HFD.
source: Comparison of the area under the curve (AUC) showed that at 18 weeks, the OCR of the Ly6Clow monocytes was significantly lowered by HFD (Figure 3I).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3I.

claim: At 8 and 18 weeks, the AUC of the OCR of the Ly6Clow monocytes was significantly higher than the AUC of the OCR of Ly6Chigh monocytes in the control group.
source: Interestingly, at 8 and 18 weeks, the AUC of the OCR of the Ly6Clow monocytes was significantly higher than the AUC of the OCR of Ly6Chigh monocytes in the control group (Figure 3H–I).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3H-I.

claim: The difference in OCR between Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes was lost in the HFD group as the AUC of the OCR of Ly6Clow monocytes diminished.
source: Moreover, this difference was lost in the HFD group as the AUC of the OCR of Ly6Clow monocytes diminished (Figure 3H–I).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3H-I.

claim: The extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) of Ly6Clow monocytes was higher than that of Ly6Chigh monocytes.
source: Conversely, the extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) of Ly6Clow monocytes was higher than that of Ly6Chigh monocytes, consistent with a more active metabolism in the former (Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3J.

claim: The difference in ECAR between monocyte subsets was lost with HFD, as ECAR dropped in the Ly6Clow monocytes and rose in the Ly6Chigh monocytes relative to the control diet group.
source: However, this difference was lost with HFD, as ECAR dropped in the Ly6Clow monocytes and rose in the Ly6Chigh monocytes relative to the control diet group (Figure 3J).
evidence: Supported by Seahorse metabolic analysis data in Figure 3J.

claim: HFD lowers OCR in Ly6Clow monocytes.
source: Overall, these results suggest that, along with promoting the preponderance of Ly6Chigh monocytes, HFD also lowers OCR in Ly6Clow monocytes.
evidence: Summary of Seahorse metabolic analysis data from Figure 3D-I.

claim: An analysis of the BM showed elevated lactate levels across all HFD time points.
source: Endorsing these results, an analysis of the BM showed elevated lactate levels across all HFD time points (Figure 3K).
evidence: Supported by lactate measurements in Figure 3K.

claim: The increase in lactate may be due to the glycolytic shift in BM monocytes.
source: This increase in lactate may be due to the glycolytic shift in BM monocytes described above, among other potential sources within the BM cellular composition.
evidence: Inferred from the observed metabolic changes in monocytes and elevated lactate levels.

claim: There were no changes between control and 18-week HFD-fed mice in pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnfα, Il1β, Il6, Cxcl1 or Ccl2 in the BM soluble fraction.
source: Further analysis of the BM soluble fraction failed to evince any changes between control and 18-week HFD-fed mice in pro-inflammatory cytokines Tnfα, Il1β, Il6, Cxcl1 or Ccl2 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: Supported by ELISA data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: There were no differences between diet groups in pro-inflammatory gene expression of Il6, Il1β or Itgax in FACS-sorted Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes.
source: Similarly, there were no differences between diet groups in pro-inflammatory gene expression of Il6, Il1β or Itgax in FACS-sorted Ly6Clow and Ly6Chigh monocytes (Not Shown).
evidence: Stated in text but data not shown in manuscript.

claim: Tnfα gene expression was higher in FACS-sorted Ly6Chigh monocytes from 18 week HFD-fed mice compared to controls.
source: However, Tnfα gene expression was higher in FACS-sorted Ly6Chigh monocytes from 18 week HFD-fed mice compared to controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: HFD alters the BM metabolic micro-environment with little effect on pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion.
source: Collectively, these findings illustrate that HFD alters the BM metabolic micro-environment with little effect on pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion (based on the panel tested).
evidence: Summary of metabolic and cytokine data from Figure 3.

claim: BM monocytes from mice fed HFD for 3 weeks did not present with differences in gene expression in the tested mitochondrial fusion genes compared to control diet counterparts.
source: BM monocytes from mice fed HFD for 3 weeks did not present with differences in gene expression in the tested mitochondrial fusion genes compared to control diet counterparts (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4A.

claim: BM monocytes isolated from mice fed HFD for 8 weeks showed downregulated Mfn1 and Mfn2 compared to the controls.
source: BM monocytes isolated from mice fed HFD for 8 weeks showed downregulated Mfn1 and Mfn2 compared to the controls (Figure 4B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4B.

claim: BM monocytes isolated from 18-week HFD-fed mice downregulated the mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn2, Opa1, and Tomm20.
source: BM monocytes isolated from 18-week HFD-fed mice downregulated the mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn2, Opa1, and Tomm20 (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4C.

claim: Drp1 was upregulated in the BM monocytes of 3 weeks HFD-fed mice.
source: Furthermore, from the tested mitochondrial fission genes, Drp1 was upregulated in the BM monocytes of 3 weeks HFD-fed mice (Figure 4D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4D.

claim: Drp1 and Ppid were upregulated in BM monocytes of 8 weeks HFD-fed mice.
source: Drp1 and Ppid were also upregulated in BM monocytes of 8 weeks HFD-fed mice (Figure 4E).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4E.

claim: At 18 weeks, all three tested mitochondrial fission genes, Drp1, Ppid, and Fis1 were upregulated.
source: At 18 weeks, all three tested mitochondrial fission genes, Drp1, Ppid, and Fis1 were upregulated (Figure 4F).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 4F.

claim: HFD skews the monocyte gene expression to favour downregulation of genes involved in mitochondrial fusion and upregulation of genes involved in fission.
source: This gene expression pattern suggests that HFD skews the monocyte gene expression to favour downregulation of genes involved in mitochondrial fusion and upregulation of genes involved in fission.
evidence: Summary of gene expression data from Figure 4A-F.

claim: The abundance of the Ly6Chigh monocyte subset negatively correlated with Mfn2 levels.
source: Indeed, and notably, the abundance of the Ly6Chigh monocyte subset negatively correlated with Mfn2 and positively correlated with Drp1 levels (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 4G.

claim: The abundance of the Ly6Chigh monocyte subset positively correlated with Drp1 levels.
source: Indeed, and notably, the abundance of the Ly6Chigh monocyte subset negatively correlated with Mfn2 and positively correlated with Drp1 levels (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 4H.

claim: The abundance of BM Ly6Clow monocytes did not correlate with the expression patterns of either Mfn2 or Drp1.
source: In contrast, the abundance of BM Ly6Clow monocytes did not correlate with the expression patterns of either Mfn2 or Drp1 (Figure 4G–H).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 4G-H.

claim: By 3 weeks into HFD, the white adipocyte marker Asc1 was significantly higher in isolated BMA from femur and tibia of HFD-fed mice relative to control diet.
source: By 3 weeks into HFD, the white adipocyte marker Asc1 (encoding the guanine nucleotide-binding protein subunit beta-like protein) was significantly higher and the brown adipocyte marker P2rx5 (encoding purinergic receptor P2X) trended to be lower albeit without reaching statistical significance, relative to control diet.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5A.

claim: By 3 weeks into HFD, the brown adipocyte marker P2rx5 trended to be lower albeit without reaching statistical significance in isolated BMA relative to control diet.
source: By 3 weeks into HFD, the white adipocyte marker Asc1 (encoding the guanine nucleotide-binding protein subunit beta-like protein) was significantly higher and the brown adipocyte marker P2rx5 (encoding purinergic receptor P2X) trended to be lower albeit without reaching statistical significance, relative to control diet.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5A.

claim: White adipocyte markers Lep and Adipoq as well as the brown adipocyte markers Ucp1 and Cdc42 did not change at 3 weeks of HFD in isolated BMA.
source: White adipocyte markers Lep (leptin) and Adipoq (adiponectin) as well as the brown adipocyte markers Ucp1 (UCP1) and Cdc42 (Pat2, Integrin alpha pat-2) did not change (Figure 5A).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5A.

claim: By 8 weeks of HFD, Asc1 mRNA remained elevated and Lep and Adipoq trended in the same direction in isolated BMA.
source: By 8 weeks of HFD, Asc1 mRNA remained elevated and Lep and Adipoq trended in the same direction (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5B.

claim: Brown adipocyte markers P2rx5 and Ucp1 in the isolated BMA of HFD mice were markedly lower relative to those from control diet mice by 8 weeks.
source: Brown adipocyte markers P2rx5 and Ucp1 in the isolated BMA of HFD mice were markedly lower relative to those from control diet mice (Figure 5B).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5B.

claim: 8 weeks of HFD sufficed to shift BMA towards white adiposity.
source: Thus, 8 weeks of HFD sufficed to shift BMA towards white adiposity.
evidence: Inferred from the gene expression changes in white and brown adipocyte markers at 8 weeks.

claim: By 18 weeks of HFD, all white adipocyte markers genes showed were upregulated while brown adipocyte markers were downregulated compared to the control group in isolated BMA.
source: By 18 weeks of HFD, all white adipocyte markers genes showed were upregulated while brown adipocyte markers were downregulated compared to the control group (Figure 5C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5C.

claim: Hoxc8 was significantly upregulated at 8 weeks of HFD in the BM pelleted fraction.
source: Hoxc8, a regulator of adipocyte progenitors (Nakagami, 2013), was significantly upregulated at 8 weeks along with Hoxc9 at 18 weeks of HFD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1B and cited reference.

claim: Hoxc9 was significantly upregulated at 18 weeks of HFD in the BM pelleted fraction.
source: Hoxc8, a regulator of adipocyte progenitors (Nakagami, 2013), was significantly upregulated at 8 weeks along with Hoxc9 at 18 weeks of HFD (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The beige adipocyte progenitor marker Tmem26 was not significantly higher at any of the tested HFD durations in the BM pelleted fraction.
source: The beige adipocyte progenitor marker Tmem26 was not significantly higher at any of the tested HFD durations (Figure 4A-C).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: Expression of the brown adipocyte determinant genes Tbx1 and Lhx8 was undetectable in the isolated BMA.
source: Expression of the brown adipocyte determinant genes Tbx1 and Lhx8 was undetectable in the isolated BMA.
evidence: Stated in text based on gene expression analysis.

claim: During the course of HFD, while markers for white adipocyte progenitor cells were upregulated, precursors of beige/brown adipocytes were not affected.
source: Thus, during the course of HFD, while markers for white adipocyte progenitor cells were upregulated, precursors of beige/brown adipocytes were not affected.
evidence: Summary of gene expression data from Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The surge in Ly6Chigh monocytes presented a significant positive correlation with Asc1 gene expression.
source: The results evinced a significant positive correlation (p value of 0.0123) for Ly6Chigh monocytes with Asc1 gene expression (Figure 5D).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 5D.

claim: The surge in Ly6Chigh monocytes presented a significant negative correlation relative to Ucp1 gene expression.
source: Conversely, the surge in Ly6Chigh monocytes presented a significant negative correlation (p value of 0.0415) relative to Ucp1 gene expression (Figure 5E).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 5E.

claim: Changes in Ly6Clow monocytes did not significantly correlate with Asc1 or Ucp1.
source: Changes in Ly6Clow monocytes did not significantly correlate with Asc1 (p value of 0.0768) or Ucp1 (p value of 0.1299) (Figure 5D–E).
evidence: Supported by correlative analysis in Figure 5D-E.

claim: BMA-CM from 3 weeks HFD-fed mice had no effect on the monocyte subset proportions compared to BMA-CM from control diet-fed mice.
source: BMA-CM from 3 weeks HFD-fed mice had no effect on the monocyte subset proportions compared to BMA-CM from control diet-fed mice (Figure 5F).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5F.

claim: BMA-CM from 8-week HFD-fed mice applied to BM-derived monocytes from control mice resulted in a significant production of Ly6Chigh monocytes compared to the effect of BMA-CM from mice on the 8-week control diet.
source: Strikingly, however, BMA-CM from 8-week HFD-fed mice applied to BM-derived monocytes from control mice resulted in a significant production of Ly6Chigh monocytes compared to the effect of BMA-CM from mice on the 8-week control diet (Figure 5G).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5G.

claim: The skewing towards Ly6Chigh monocytes was further enhanced when exposing the control BM cells to BMA-CM from 18-week HFD-fed mice.
source: This skewing was further enhanced when exposing the control BM cells to BMA-CM from 18-week HFD-fed mice (Figure 5H).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 5H.

claim: Monocytes treated with BMA-CM from HFD-fed mice for 18 weeks showed significant downregulated mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn2, Tomm20, and Tomm40.
source: Monocytes treated with BMA-CM from HFD-fed mice for 18 weeks showed significant downregulated mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn2, Tomm20, and Tomm40 (Figure 5I).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5I.

claim: The mitochondrial fission genes Drp1 and Ppid were significantly up-regulated in monocytes treated with HFD-derived BMA-CM.
source: Conversely, the mitochondrial fission genes Drp1 and Ppid were significantly up-regulated in monocytes treated with HFD-derived BMA-CM (Figure 5J).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 5J.

claim: HFD-derived BMA-CM can bias monocyte subset cellularity.
source: These results not only show that HFD-derived BMA-CM can bias monocyte subset cellularity but also can alter mitochondrial morphology via changes in mitochondrial dynamic gene expression.
evidence: Summary of flow cytometry and gene expression data from Figure 5F-J.

claim: HFD-derived BMA-CM can alter mitochondrial morphology via changes in mitochondrial dynamic gene expression.
source: These results not only show that HFD-derived BMA-CM can bias monocyte subset cellularity but also can alter mitochondrial morphology via changes in mitochondrial dynamic gene expression.
evidence: Summary of gene expression data from Figure 5I-J.

claim: WATA-CM favoured Ly6Chigh monocyte predominance.
source: These results indicate that WATA-CM favoured Ly6Chigh monocyte predominance, while BATA-CM prompted Ly6Clow monocyte abundance (Figure 6A–B), presenting a novel, differential influence of white and brown adipocytes on monocyte orientation preference.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A-B.

claim: BATA-CM prompted Ly6Clow monocyte abundance.
source: These results indicate that WATA-CM favoured Ly6Chigh monocyte predominance, while BATA-CM prompted Ly6Clow monocyte abundance (Figure 6A–B), presenting a novel, differential influence of white and brown adipocytes on monocyte orientation preference.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 6A-B.

claim: Ly6Clow monocytes incubated in vitro with WATA-CM experienced a left-ward shift in MitoTracker Red CMXRos peak indicating a reduction in mitochondrial membrane potential induced by the WATA-CM.
source: Remarkably, Ly6Clow monocytes incubated in vitro with WATA-CM experienced a left-ward shift in MitoTracker Red CMXRos peak indicating a reduction in mitochondrial membrane potential induced by the WATA-CM (Figure 6C), reproducing what was observed with monocytes from HFD-fed mice (see Figure 3A–C).
evidence: Supported by MitoTracker Red CMXRos flow cytometry data in Figure 6C.

claim: The gene expression of mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn1, Mfn2, Tomm20, and Tomm40 were reduced in monocytes treated with WATA-CM.
source: Furthermore, the gene expression of mitochondrial fusion genes Mfn1, Mfn2, Tomm20, and Tomm40 were reduced in monocytes treated with WATA-CM (Figure 6D).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 6D.

claim: The mitochondrial fission genes Drp1, Ppid and Fis1 were up-regulated in monocytes treated with WATA-CM.
source: The mitochondrial fission genes Drp1, Ppid and Fis1 were up-regulated in monocytes treated with WATA-CM (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 6E.

claim: Treating monocytes with BATA-CM downregulated the mitochondrial fission gene Ppid.
source: Conversely, treating monocytes with BATA-CM downregulated the mitochondrial fission gene Ppid (Figure 6E).
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 6E.

claim: WATA-CM induced a striking increase in the percentage of cells with fragmented mitochondria, from 22% in control CM-treated cells to 64%.
source: WATA-CM induced a striking increase in the percentage of cells with fragmented mitochondria, from 22% in control CM-treated cells to 64%.
evidence: Supported by super-resolution microscopy data in Figure 6F-H.

claim: BATA-CM raised mitochondrial elongation from 20% in CM-treated cells to 55%.
source: On the other hand, BATA-CM raised mitochondrial elongation from 20% in CM-treated cells to 55% (Figure 6F–H).
evidence: Supported by super-resolution microscopy data in Figure 6F-H.

claim: White adipocyte products alter the metabolic status of Ly6Clow monocytes by reducing their mitochondrial membrane potential and altering mitochondrial dynamic gene expression and morphology.
source: These observations suggest that white adipocyte products alter the metabolic status of Ly6Clow monocytes by reducing their mitochondrial membrane potential and altering mitochondrial dynamic gene expression and morphology, thereby linking changes in BMA whitening to monocyte metabolic status.
evidence: Summary of data from Figure 6C-H.

claim: The shift to mitochondrial fragmentation coincided with the higher abundance Ly6Chigh monocytes resulting from in vitro-generated monocytes with WATA-CM.
source: Moreover, the shift to mitochondrial fragmentation coincided with the higher abundance Ly6Chigh monocytes resulting from in vitro-generated monocytes with WATA-CM (Figure 6A and B).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry and microscopy data in Figure 6A, B, F-H.

claim: A small gain in myeloid progenitor cell (CMP) was observed in response to WATA-CM treatment.
source: Surveying several cell populations, only a small gain in myeloid progenitor cell (CMP) was observed in response to WATA-CM treatment (Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1A-C.

claim: GMP cells did not become more abundant with WATA-CM treatment, even though content of CMP, their upstream multipotential progenitors, was slightly elevated.
source: GMP cells are downstream of CMP during lineage progression of progenitor cells towards monocytes or erythroid cells (Yáñez et al., 2017), and so it is noteworthy these cells did not become more abundant with WATA-CM treatment, even though content of CMP, their upstream multipotential progenitors, was slightly elevated (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C and cited reference.

claim: WATA-CM-treated monocytes rendered the expected increase in Ly6Chigh monocytes, yet these cells did not show significantly higher incorporation of BrdU than untreated controls.
source: WATA-CM-treated monocytes rendered the expected increase in Ly6Chigh monocytes, yet these cells did not show significantly higher incorporation of BrdU than untreated controls, implying that they are not actively replicating their DNA (Figure 7A,B).
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation flow cytometry data in Figure 7A-B.

claim: BATA-CM increased DNA-incorporated BrdU in the sorted Ly6Clow monocyte subset.
source: In contrast, BATA-CM increased DNA-incorporated BrdU in the sorted Ly6Clow monocyte subset, visualized as yellow to red hues in the CD11b+ Ly6Clow cell gate (Figure 7A), and the number of proliferating cells was elevated by 25-fold (Figure 7B).
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation flow cytometry data in Figure 7A-B.

claim: Brown adipocytes promote an abundance of Ly6Clow monocytes by inducing their proliferation.
source: These findings revealed that brown adipocytes promote an abundance of Ly6Clow monocytes by inducing their proliferation.
evidence: Summary of BrdU incorporation data from Figure 7A-B.

claim: BATA-CM promoted growth of CMP/CFU-GEMM cultures over control Media.
source: BATA-CM promoted growth of CMP/CFU-GEMM cultures over control Media (**p<0.01 Two-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparisons, Figure 7C) and biased granulocyte/macrophage progenitors (widely known as GMP) towards macrophage over granulocyte differentiation, relative to control Media (**p<0.01) or WATA-CM (*p<0.05 or ***p<0.001, Figure 7C).
evidence: Supported by colony forming unit assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: BATA-CM biased granulocyte/macrophage progenitors towards macrophage over granulocyte differentiation, relative to control Media or WATA-CM.
source: BATA-CM promoted growth of CMP/CFU-GEMM cultures over control Media (**p<0.01 Two-way ANOVA, Tukey's multiple comparisons, Figure 7C) and biased granulocyte/macrophage progenitors (widely known as GMP) towards macrophage over granulocyte differentiation, relative to control Media (**p<0.01) or WATA-CM (*p<0.05 or ***p<0.001, Figure 7C).
evidence: Supported by colony forming unit assay data in Figure 7C.

claim: The total numbers of colonies that grew after 7–10 days of culturing of each pre-treated cohort of monocytes were not different across the three treatments, although trended upwards with BATA-CM.
source: The total numbers of colonies that grew after 7–10 days of culturing of each pre-treated cohort of monocytes were not different across the three treatments, although trended upwards with BATA-CM (Figure 7D).
evidence: Supported by colony forming unit assay data in Figure 7D.

claim: While BATA-CM promoted expansion of selected populations (CMP/CFU-GEMM and CFU-M), WATA-CM was without effect relative to control Media.
source: These results indicated that while BATA-CM promoted expansion of selected populations (CMP/CFU-GEMM and CFU-M), consistent with the increase in BrdU incorporation shown above, WATA-CM was without effect relative to control Media.
evidence: Summary of colony forming unit assay data from Figure 7C-D.

claim: GMP progenitor cells were essentially the only progenitors detected in the Ly6Clow monocyte subset, and they represented 140 GMP per 1000 Ly6Clow cells.
source: GMP progenitor cells were essentially the only progenitors detected by this approach in the Ly6Clow monocyte subset, and they represented 140 GMP per 1000 Ly6Clow cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 7E.

claim: WATA-CM treatment did not result in an appreciable expansion of progenitor cells or colony formation.
source: Collectively, the results in Figure 7C–E indicate that WATA-CM treatment did not result in an appreciable expansion of progenitor cells or colony formation.
evidence: Summary of data from Figure 7C-E.

claim: No conversion from Ly6Chigh to Ly6Clow monocytes was observed in any condition.
source: Surprisingly, no conversion from Ly6Chigh (red) to Ly6Clow (gray) monocytes was observed in any condition (Figure 8A–F), but, remarkably, there was a switch of the FACS sorted Ly6Clow into Ly6Chigh monocytes following exposure to WATA-CM (Figure 8B and E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 8A-F.

claim: There was a switch of the FACS sorted Ly6Clow into Ly6Chigh monocytes following exposure to WATA-CM.
source: Surprisingly, no conversion from Ly6Chigh (red) to Ly6Clow (gray) monocytes was observed in any condition (Figure 8A–F), but, remarkably, there was a switch of the FACS sorted Ly6Clow into Ly6Chigh monocytes following exposure to WATA-CM (Figure 8B and E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 8B and E.

claim: Following the 18 hr WATA-CM treatment, the monocyte population consisted of 49.7% Ly6Chigh monocytes (and correspondingly only Ly6Clow monocytes 50.3%).
source: While the FACS-sorted starting cells were all Ly6Clow monocytes, following the 18 hr WATA-CM treatment the monocyte population consisted of 49.7% Ly6Chigh monocytes (and correspondingly only Ly6Clow monocytes 50.3%) (Figure 8E).
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 8E.

claim: All other isolated cell and CM treatment combinations tested gave rise to a maximum of 16.3% of the opposite monocyte subset compared to the starting population.
source: This was in stark contrast to all other isolated cell and CM treatment combinations tested, which gave rise to a maximum of 16.3% of the opposite monocyte subset compared to the starting population.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 8A-F.

claim: There is a temporal correlation between HFD-induced whitening of BMA and a BM myeloid lineage bias towards Ly6Chigh-bearing monocytes in vivo.
source: In this study, we demonstrate a temporal correlation between HFD-induced whitening of BMA and a BM myeloid lineage bias towards Ly6Chigh-bearing monocytes in vivo.
evidence: Summary of in vivo data from Figures 2, 4, and 5.

claim: Ly6Chigh monocytes presented a more glycolytic metabolism underpinned by a reduction in mitochondrial membrane potential, a rise in mitochondrial fission genes and a reduction in mitochondrial fusion genes.
source: The latter presented a more glycolytic metabolism underpinned by a reduction in mitochondrial membrane potential, a rise in mitochondrial fission genes and a reduction in mitochondrial fusion genes.
evidence: Summary of metabolic and gene expression data from Figures 3 and 4.

claim: CM from BMA of HFD-fed mice promotes the generation of Ly6Chigh monocytes ex vivo.
source: Causatively, we show that CM from BMA of HFD-fed mice promotes the generation of Ly6Chigh monocytes ex vivo.
evidence: Supported by ex vivo experiments in Figure 5F-H.

claim: White adipocytes induced a shift in monocyte subset proportion, from Ly6Clow to Ly6Chigh, suggesting a possible and novel conversion of one subset into the other.
source: Mechanistically, white adipocytes induced a shift in monocyte subset proportion, from Ly6Clow to Ly6Chigh, suggesting a possible and novel conversion of one subset into the other, while brown adipocytes favoured Ly6Clow predominance by inducing their proliferation.
evidence: Supported by flow cytometry data in Figures 6, 7, and 8.

claim: Brown adipocytes favoured Ly6Clow predominance by inducing their proliferation.
source: Mechanistically, white adipocytes induced a shift in monocyte subset proportion, from Ly6Clow to Ly6Chigh, suggesting a possible and novel conversion of one subset into the other, while brown adipocytes favoured Ly6Clow predominance by inducing their proliferation.
evidence: Supported by BrdU incorporation and colony forming unit assay data in Figure 7.

claim: WATA blunted the monocyte's mitochondrial membrane potential and OCR.
source: These changes in monocytes were underpinned by alterations in the monocytes metabolism, as WATA blunted the monocyte's mitochondrial membrane potential and OCR.
evidence: Supported by MitoTracker and Seahorse data in Figure 6C.

claim: BMA are not mere space fillers, rather they are important contributors to cellular metabolism and hematopoietic lineage decisions.
source: Along with the observation of dynamic whitening of BMA during HFD, our results contribute to the emerging evidence that BMA are not mere space fillers, rather they are important contributors to cellular metabolism and hematopoietic lineage decisions (Boroumand and Klip, 2020).
evidence: Inferred from the study's findings and cited reference.

claim: The BM is an early responder to a change in feeding status.
source: That these changes occur early on in the course of diet-induced obesity suggests that the BM is an early responder to a change in feeding status and that adipocytes play a significant role in directing monocyte subset skewing.
evidence: Inferred from the temporal data showing BM changes at 3 weeks of HFD.

claim: Adipocytes play a significant role in directing monocyte subset skewing.
source: That these changes occur early on in the course of diet-induced obesity suggests that the BM is an early responder to a change in feeding status and that adipocytes play a significant role in directing monocyte subset skewing.
evidence: Inferred from the ex vivo experiments showing adipocyte CM effects on monocytes.

claim: Singer et al., 2014 demonstrated that transplantation of BM from 18week HFD-fed mice into control recipients increased the number of invasive circulating monocytes and pro-inflammatory AT macrophages.
source: Singer et al., 2014 demonstrated that transplantation of BM from 18week HFD-fed mice into control recipients increased the number of invasive circulating monocytes and pro-inflammatory AT macrophages.
evidence: Cited from Singer et al., 2014 study.

claim: HFD influences hematopoietic myeloid bias in the BM upstream of monocyte tissue invasion, thereby contributing to downstream systemic and peripheral tissue inflammation.
source: These pioneering findings heralded the notion that HFD influences hematopoietic myeloid bias in the BM upstream of monocyte tissue invasion, thereby contributing to downstream systemic and peripheral tissue inflammation.
evidence: Inferred from Singer et al., 2014 findings and the current study's data.

claim: Total BM monocytes increase by 3 weeks of HFD, whereas the proportion of Ly6Chigh monocyte predominance was evident only at 8 weeks coinciding with a gain in AT macrophages that were also pro-inflammatory skewed.
source: In the present study, by analyzing chronological changes in EWAT and BM myeloid composition, we observed that total BM monocytes increase by 3 weeks of HFD, whereas the proportion of Ly6Chigh monocyte predominance was evident only at 8 weeks coinciding with a gain in AT macrophages that were also pro-inflammatory skewed.
evidence: Summary of flow cytometry data from Figure 2.

claim: The rise in total monocytes observed at 3 weeks of HFD and prior to elevation of AT macrophages identifies the BM as an earlier-responding locus during HFD.
source: The rise in total monocytes observed at 3 weeks of HFD and prior to elevation of AT macrophages identifies the BM as an earlier-responding locus during HFD.
evidence: Inferred from the temporal data in Figure 2.

claim: At 3 weeks of HFD, only Ly6Clow monocytes are elevated in the BM.
source: Therefore, it appears that only Ly6Clow monocytes are elevated in the BM at 3 weeks of HFD.
evidence: Inferred from flow cytometry data in Figure 2J.

claim: By 8 weeks, the BM has adopted the 'typical' HFD-induced hematopoietic phenotype, showing increased Ly6Chigh monocytes.
source: By 8 weeks of HFD, we observed a shift in the monocyte subset proportion, favouring Ly6Chigh monocytes. Thus, by 8 weeks, the BM has adopted the 'typical' HFD-induced hematopoietic phenotype, in so far as it already shows the increased Ly6Chigh monocytes previously reported at the habitually studied 16–18 weeks of HFD.
evidence: Inferred from flow cytometry data in Figure 2J and comparison to literature.

claim: Singer et al. found progenitor cells elevated at 16 weeks of HFD but not at 6 weeks, yet an increase in circulating Ly6Chigh monocytes was already observed at 6 weeks.
source: However, in the latter study, at 6 weeks of HFD, they did not observe changes in progenitor populations, yet an increase in circulating Ly6Chigh monocytes was already observed (Figure 5C in Singer et al., 2015).
evidence: Cited from Singer et al., 2015 study.

claim: Progenitor proliferation may be dissociated from the time during HFD when the specification leading to the increase in proportion of the Ly6Chigh subset takes place.
source: Collectively, those key studies and ours suggest the possibility that progenitor proliferation may be dissociated from the time during HFD when the specification leading to the increase in proportion of the Ly6Chigh subset takes place.
evidence: Inferred from the current study's data and Singer et al. studies.

claim: A gain in pro-inflammatory AT macrophages by 8 weeks of HFD is concurrent with the predominance of invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes in the BM.
source: By comparison, we detected a gain in pro-inflammatory AT macrophages by 8 weeks of HFD that is concurrent with the predominance of invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes in the BM.
evidence: Summary of flow cytometry data from Figure 2.

claim: The embryonic-derived tissue resident AT macrophage markers, Timd4 and Marco, were not elevated until 18 weeks of HFD.
source: In contrast, the embryonic-derived tissue resident AT macrophage markers, Timd4 and Marco (Beattie et al., 2016; Gibbings et al., 2015), were not elevated until 18 weeks of HFD.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data in Figure 2G-H and cited references.

claim: The contribution of the BM-derived myeloid cell pool to early EWAT pathology and AT macrophage accumulation is important.
source: This brings to light the importance of the contribution of the BM-derived myeloid cell pool to early EWAT pathology and AT macrophage accumulation.
evidence: Inferred from the temporal data showing BM changes precede AT macrophage accumulation.

claim: BMA are a distinctive member of the BM cellular suite that is sensitive to HFD effects.
source: BMA are a distinctive member of the BM cellular suite that is sensitive to HFD effects (Pham et al., 2020).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by cited reference.

claim: In lean mice, BMA present characteristics that are similar to those of beige or brown adipocytes in peripheral AT.
source: In lean mice, BMA present characteristics that are similar to those of beige or brown adipocytes in peripheral AT (Cuminetti and Arranz, 2019).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by cited reference.

claim: With HFD, BMA undergo hyperplasia and hypertrophy triggered by PPARγ activation.
source: With HFD, BMA undergo hyperplasia and hypertrophy triggered by PPARγ activation (Rosen and MacDougald, 2006).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by cited reference.

claim: With obesity, adipocyte precursor mesenchymal stem cells tilt their lineage commitment towards adipogenesis.
source: Furthermore, with obesity, adipocyte precursor mesenchymal stem cells tilt their lineage commitment towards adipogenesis (da Silva et al., 2016; Bowers and Singer, 2021).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by cited references.

claim: Brown adipocyte markers of BMA are reduced in obese mice and a parallel adoption of more white adipocyte markers has been observed.
source: Brown adipocyte markers of BMA are reduced in obese mice and a parallel adoption of more white adipocyte markers has been observed (Adler et al., 2014; Doucette et al., 2015; Krings et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in text and supported by cited references.

claim: Obesity-induced gains in whole body adiposity was causally linked to elevated circulating CD11b+ monocytes.
source: Obesity-induced gains in whole body adiposity was causally linked to elevated circulating CD11b+ monocytes (Takahashi et al., 2003).
evidence: Cited from Takahashi et al., 2003 study.

claim: The rise in BM Ly6Chigh monocytes and the shift in BMA whitening both manifested by 8 weeks of HFD.
source: The rise in BM Ly6Chigh monocytes and the shift in BMA whitening both manifested by 8 weeks of HFD.
evidence: Summary of data from Figures 2 and 5.

claim: The mere shift in BMA towards white adiposity may directly favour induction of BM Ly6Chigh monocytes.
source: Collectively, the above data suggest the possibility that the mere shift in BMA towards white adiposity may directly favour induction of BM Ly6Chigh monocytes.
evidence: Inferred from correlative analysis in Figure 5D-E.

claim: HFD-induced remodelling in BMA disrupts the normal balance of BM monocyte subsets leading to a higher output of tissue invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes.
source: We propose that HFD-induced remodelling in BMA disrupts the normal balance of BM monocyte subsets leading to a higher output of tissue invasive Ly6Chigh monocytes.
evidence: Summary of all findings from the study.
